title: I Added Portals to Chess
summary: Portal chess vs Stockfish (sequel to 'Chess, But I Can Use Portals', now playable on iwantcheckmate.com). The player can place a pair of linked portals (blue + orange, Portal-game style) on any squares: double-left-click places the blue portal, double-right-click the orange. A piece moving onto one portal exits from the other, so pieces can be teleported across the board (e.g. a rook entering e1 emerges on a8 for mate). The engine doesn't use portals. Narrator wins game one with portal-rook mate on a8, then tries to win in under 15 moves.
rules: Standard chess start; player White vs Stockfish (3600).
Player can place/reposition a blue portal (double left-click) and an orange portal (double right-click) on squares; only one of each exists at a time.
Portal placement appears to be free (no move cost) and can be changed every turn [inferred from 'set up a portal on E1, set the location portal at A8, and then rook to E1 is simply checkmate'].
A piece that moves onto a portal square is teleported to the other portal's square (capturing/attacking there as if it had moved there); a check delivered from the exit square counts.
Only the player uses portals; Stockfish plays normal chess (it doesn't anticipate them).
